summary: Embed reply reordering + client retry storm causing rerank top-k instability and latency spikes
description:
Issue summary:
VaultSearch reported intermittent rerank quality regressions and p95/p99 tail latency spikes for their search rerank endpoint starting 2026-03-09 18:00 UTC. Symptoms include missing expected top-k items (customers see different top-k on repeated queries), and end-to-end p95 increasing from ~120ms to >2s in bursts.

Impact:
- Production search degraded for ~40% of VaultSearch requests during burst windows; some queries returned incomplete candidate sets.
- Customer-facing product observed transient relevance regression and increased error/retry rates.

Environment:
- Product: VaultSearch internal search (enterprise dedicated tenant)
- Region: us-west-2
- Components: client -> API Gateway (ALB) -> proxy-sidecar (envoy) -> embed-service -> reranker -> serving-runtime
- Model versions: redwood-embed-512@v6, rerank-linear-v2@stable

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Run 50 concurrent search requests with small candidate pools (~100 candidates) and a client-side retry policy (retry on 5xx/tcp timeout with 2s backoff).
2) Observe intermittent queries where top-5 is missing expected items or contains duplicates.
3) Measure p95 latency across both embed and rerank phases; spikes align with retry bursts.

Observed behavior:
- Embed responses occasionally arrive late relative to rerank inputs (out-of-order ingestion).
- Retries from client produce duplicate request IDs visible in logs and sometimes lead to partial candidate merges.
- When embed-service experiences transient CPU saturation, scheduler starts to queue requests; queue reordering combined with client retries results in reranker consuming a mixture of old and new candidate embeddings (leading to top-k instability).

Expected behavior:
- Idempotent retries should either be deduplicated upstream or processed in strict request order such that reranker sees a consistent candidate set. Latency should remain within SLOs and top-k should be stable across quick replays.

Relevant logs/traces attached:
- API Gateway traces show clusters of retried requests with identical client-generated request_id header between 2026-03-09T18:12:30Z and 18:18:00Z.
- Envoy sidecar metrics show transmit queue growth and occasional 429s from embed-service.
- Reranker logs show candidate list sizes fluctuating and several warnings about "stale-embed-ids".

Initial hypothesis summary:
- Client retry pattern + embed-service backpressure caused interleaving of in-flight requests such that the reranker consumed partial/duplicate candidate sets.
- Deduplication is not applied consistently because request-id semantics were changed in a previous patch (see linked PR) and the proxy rewrites part of the header in rare TCP retransmit windows.

Priority/Next steps:
- Contain: advise customer to temporarily disable aggressive client retries and switch to linear backoff (Support action).
- Mitigate: enable strict-ordering flag on the embed-service for VaultSearch tenant (config change) to force FIFO processing while we diagnose.
- Investigate: SRE to correlate scheduler queues, and Eng to audit request-id handling in the proxy and embed ingress.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:20 - Support (Ava Patel): Received report from VaultSearch. Customer provides request samples and trace IDs. Assigned to Marcus for initial triage.

2026-03-10 10:05 - SRE (Marcus Nguyen): Confirmed burst of identical request_id header values; saw embed-service cpu queue growth coincident with spike. Recommending customer reduce retry aggressiveness while we investigate.

2026-03-10 11:30 - Customer (VaultSearch - Lina Chen): We've applied a temporary disable for automatic retries and saw a reduction in latency spikes in the next hour; however, top-k still occasionally differs. We can run additional traces on demand.

2026-03-10 14:12 - Eng (Diego Alvarez): Found a code path in ingress-proxy that rewrites request_id when connection resets are handled. Opening PR to preserve original request_id on retransmit. Also started a quick audit for dedup keys in embed-service.

2026-03-11 08:50 - SRE (Marcus Nguyen): Rolled out tenant-scoped strict-ordering config for VaultSearch at 2026-03-11T08:30Z. Early metrics show decreased top-k instability and fewer duplicate candidates. Still monitoring p99.

2026-03-12 09:15 - Support (Ava Patel): Customer confirmed improved stability after strict-ordering toggle and client retry tuning. Awaiting Eng PR merge for permanent fix and a follow-up window for a controlled rollback test.\n
investigation: 2026-03-10 - Correlated API traces with embed-service CPU metrics; queueing coincides with retry storms from customer-side load tests.
2026-03-10 - Reproduced locally by simulating client retries + induced 200ms CPU sleep in embed worker; observed reranker consuming interleaved candidate batches leading to top-k variance.
2026-03-10 - Audited ingress-proxy: identified header rewrite behavior during connection reset branch (edge case) which caused multiple requests to share identical dedup tokens intermittently.
2026-03-11 - Confirmed tenant-scoped strict-ordering prevents premature dequeueing; however it adds tail latency under sustained load, so we need a targeted fix in ingress-proxy dedup logic.
2026-03-11 - Cross-referenced with SUP-331210 where similar out-of-order symptoms were traced to proxy-sidecar rotation; patterns differ but useful artifacts exist in that ticket.
resolution: Workaround applied: tenant-scoped strict-ordering enabled for VaultSearch and customer reduced client retry aggressiveness. Observed immediate improvement in top-k stability and reduced p95 spikes.

Root cause (preliminary): ingress-proxy retransmit handling could rewrite or nullify client-provided request_id under TCP reset conditions; combined with client retries this created duplicate dedup keys and allowed interleaving of old/new candidate sets.

Permanent fix: Eng to merge PR that preserves request_id across retransmit and to add explicit dedup token validation at embed-service ingress (PR #849). Rollout plan: canary in us-west-2 single AZ, monitor queue length and top-k error rate, then wider rollout. Target date: 2026-03-17.

Post-incident actions: update runbook to include steps to toggle tenant strict-ordering, add telemetry to detect identical request_id storm patterns, and add a test in CI to simulate client retry + reset scenarios.
Customer communication: scheduled follow-up call on 2026-03-13 to review root cause and rollout schedule.
